newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia sees 4-5 pct GDP to 2002, balanced budget.
newsitem.headline: Latvia sees 4-5 pct GDP to 2002, balanced budget.

text.p: Latvia's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to grow an average annual 4-5 percent to the year 2002 and, in that time, the government wants to keep a balanced budget, the finance ministry said on Friday.

"We are looking forward to stable development with four to five percent GDP growth on average until 2002," Inna Steinbuka, deputy head of the finance ministry's planning department, told a news conference.
Finance Minister Robert Zile said Latvia planned a balanced budget until 2002 but some deficit may be allowed if state investment projects were necessary.
But he said any state investment would not be more than 0.5 percent of gross domestic product.
"It is agreed upon also by the International Monetary Fund," Zile told a news conference.
"We aim to meet all the Maastricht criteria by 2002," Zile added.
Latvia had a balanced central government last year and has set one again this year. It is considering the drafting of a two-year budget for 1998 and 1998.
"Inflation still causes problems but we have the means to reduce it," Zile added.
Steinbuka said inflation was forecast to be seven percent in 1998, eight percent in 1999, 6.8 percent in 2000 and 5.8 percent in 2001.
"we are especially taking into account energy, gas, heating, rent and transport expenses," she said.
